records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14; app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — Cache misses enqueue retrieval jobs before throttling, and per-full-URL throttling can be bypassed by spoofing Referer and varying query strings to flood Sidekiq.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) whenever TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns nil, with no rate limiting at the controller; throttling (retrieved_recently? with redis setnx keyed on the full embed_url) happens only inside TopicRetriever#retrieve, after the job is enqueued. Since the cache lookup and throttle key both use the full embed_url, an attacker varying query strings floods Sidekiq with enqueued jobs, and the 60-second throttle never trips because each distinct URL gets its own key. records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42-45 — The spec expects synchronous `TopicRetriever` instantiation and invocation even though the implementation enqueues `:retrieve_topic`, so it fails and does not test the actual asynchronous behavior.
records.rationale: embed_controller.rb calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) rather than instantiating TopicRetriever synchronously; the spec (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42-45) expects TopicRetriever.new and retriever.receive/retrieve, which the controller never calls, so the 'tells the topic retriever to work' spec fails and does not exercise the actual enqueue behavior.
